The petitioner has called in question the legality and validity of the communication dated 17.03.2023, issued by respondent No.2 (Annexure-K), whereby, the offer of appointment dated 02.11.2022 to the post of the Assistant Professor, Grade-I, Chemistry at IIT-Dharwad has been withdrawn, after the petitioner had already accepted the offer, joined duty and disclosed all material facts relating to the criminal proceedings pending against him.

Brief facts:
2. The petitioner, a highly qualified academician with international research experience, applied pursuant to a recruitment notification issued by the respondent-institute.
After due selection process, interview, and approval by the competent authority, an offer of appointment dated 02.11.2022 was issued in his favour.

The petitioner NC: 2026:KHC-D:1686 HC-KAR accepted the offer, resigned from his earlier employment, joined duty on 15.02.2023 and submitted a prescribed attestation form on 28.02.2023, wherein he truthfully disclosed the pendency of a criminal case and his arrest and custody arising out of a matrimonial dispute with his wife.

Despite such disclosure, without issuing a show cause notice or affording an opportunity of hearing, the respondent issued the impugned communication (Annexure- K), withdrawing the appointment solely on the ground of pendency of the criminal case.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the impugned action is arbitrary, disproportionate and violative of the principles of natural justice, as no opportunity of hearing was afforded prior to withdrawal of the appointment.
The petitioner has not suppressed any material fact, on the contrary he made a full and truthful disclosure in the attestation form.

It is submitted that the respondent has misapplied the statutory scheme and the judicial precedents governing verification of antecedents.

4. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent submits that the service matters of IIT are governed by the Institutes of Technology Act, 1961 ('Act 1961' for short) and the First Statutes of IIT Dharwad 2017, appointments/action must conform to the statutory NC: 2026:KHC-D:1686 HC-KAR provision.

It is submitted that Section 19 of the First Statutes governs conditions of service,
discipline and suspension.
Schedule C, clause 16(b) permits placing an employee under suspension where a criminal case is under investigation/trial.
Clause 16(b) bars assignment of duties to staff facing criminal investigation.

It is submitted that in the attestation, the petitioner disclosed arrest,
detention and pendency of a criminal case and, given the serious of allegation and the statutory scheme, the Institute states that joining was not complete until verification and hence the offer was withdrawn on 17.03.2023 after verification.

sentences.text: In this context, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the respondents have failed to point out any provision under the Act, 1961 or the First Statutes of IIT Dharwad 2017, which authorizes withdrawal of appointments solely on the ground of a criminal case.

On the contrary,
Section 19 read with "Schedule C", clause 16(a) and (b) only contemplate suspension or regulation of duties, and not cancellation of appointment, and thus the impugned action travels beyond the statutory framework and is ultra vires.
He submits that mere arrest or pendency of a proceedings purely matrimonial in nature, cannot be equated with unsuitability especially when the statutory rules do not prescribe such consequence.

He further submits that the petitioner has truthfully disclosed all material particulars in attestation form and once the disclosure is honest, the respondents were required to undertake an objective assessment of suitability as mandated by law.
Mechanical withdrawal of appointment defeats the very purpose of antecedent verification.
Thus NC: 2026:KHC-D:1686 HC-KAR submits that such a plea cannot substitute the statutory compliance.

This Court has carefully considered the rival submissions and perused the material on record.

The point that arise for consideration in this Writ Petition is, "Whether the respondents were justified in withdrawing the petitioner's appointment solely on the basis of pendency of a matrimonial criminal case and is it sustainable in law under the governing statutory rules?"
8.
The service conditions of the IIT Dharwad are governed by the Act, 1961 and the First Statues of the Indian Institute of Technology, Dharwad, 2017.

Section 19 of the Service of Conditions reads thus:
"19. Terms and Conditions of Service of the Employees and Determining their Seniority (1) There shall be the following categories of employees of the Institute - a) Permanent Employees b) Temporary Employees NC: 2026:KHC-D:1686 HC-KAR c) Employees on Contract The terms and conditions of service for each of the above categories shall be as provided in the Schedule B. (2) For determining the inter-se seniority of employees of different categories for specific purposes such as for the membership of authorities and bodies, residential accommodation etc, the Board may approve the norms and guidelines from time to time.
(3) The employees shall be governed by the Conduct Rules as detailed in the Schedule C."
9. Schedule C, clause 16 discipline and conduct reads thus:
"16 Disciplinary action:
Suspension: The Director may place a member of the staff appointed at the Institute under suspension:
(a) where a disciplinary proceeding against him contemplated or is pending; or NC:
2026:KHC-D:1686 HC-KAR (b) where a case in respect of any criminal offence is under investigation or trial"
10.

A conjoint reading of Act, 1961 and Section 19 read with Schedule C, clause 16(a) and (b) of the First Statues of the Indian Institute of Technology Dharwad, 2017 makes it manifest clear that the statutory scheme does not confer any power on the respondents to withdraw or cancel an appointment solely on the ground of a pendency of a criminal case.

Under the governing rules,
pendency of a criminal proceedings is recognized only Laxman Gouda S/O Kesha Gouda vs The Director on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13363817/

sentences.text: The Statue does not contemplate withdrawal of appointment, cancellation of selection or termination of service as an automatic or a consequential measure on mere pendency of a criminal proceedings.

When the statute expressly provides for a lesser and temporary measures, the respondents could not have - 10 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:1686 HC-KAR resorted to a most drastic action which is neither contemplated nor sanctioned by the Rules.

11. Further, what is important to be noted is the criminal case relied upon by the respondents arises out of a matrimonial dispute initiated by the wife and does not relate to any offence involving moral turpitude or professional misconduct, financial impropriety or violation of any statutory obligation attached to the post of Assistant Professor.
Such proceedings, by their very nature, do not constitute a statutory disqualification under the applicable rules or which was within the wisdom of the administration.

In the absence of any express rule enabling withdrawal of appointment, the impugned action is ultra vires the statutory framework and cannot be sustained merely on the basis of administrative discretion or legal opinion.

Accordingly, this Court holds that the respondent lacked rule based authority to withdraw the petitioners' appointment and the impugned communication dated 17.03.2023 is therefore illegal and unsustainable in law.

In case there is suppression or false information of involvement in a criminal case where conviction or acquittal had already been recorded before filling of the application/verification form and such fact later comes to knowledge of employer, any of the following recourses appropriate to the case may be adopted:
38.4.1.

In a case trivial in nature in which conviction had been recorded, such as shouting slogans at young age or for a petty offence which if disclosed would not have rendered an incumbent unfit for post in question, the employer may, in its discretion,
ignore such suppression of fact or false information by condoning the lapse.

38.4.2. Where conviction has been recorded in case which is not trivial in nature,
employer may cancel candidature or terminate services of the employee.

If acquittal had already been recorded in a case involving moral turpitude or offence of heinous/serious nature, on technical ground and it is not a case of clean acquittal, or benefit of reasonable doubt has been given, the employer may consider all relevant facts available as to antecedents, and may take appropriate decision as to the continuance of the employee.
In a case where the employee has made declaration truthfully of a concluded criminal case, the employer still has the right to consider antecedents, and cannot be compelled to appoint the candidate.

38.6. In case when fact has been truthfully declared in character verification form regarding pendency of a criminal case of trivial nature, employer, in facts and circumstances of the case, in its discretion, may appoint the candidate subject to decision of such case.

38.7. In a case of deliberate suppression of fact with respect to multiple pending cases such false information by itself will assume significance and an employer may pass appropriate order cancelling candidature or terminating services as appointment of a person against whom multiple criminal cases were pending may not be proper.

38.8. If criminal case was pending but not known to the candidate at the time of filling the form, still it may have adverse impact and the appointing authority would take decision after considering the seriousness of the crime.

ORDER i. The writ petition is allowed.
ii.

The impugned communication dated 17.03.2023 passed by respondent No.2 withdrawing the petitioner's appointment dated 02.11.2022 to the post of Assistant Professor, Grade-I, Chemistry is hereby quashed.

iii. The withdrawal of appointment cannot be constituted as valid, as the pendency of a criminal case arising out of the matrimonial dispute in the absence of any statutory qualification under the Institute of Technology Act, 1961 and Section 19 read with Section C, clause 16(a) and (b) of the first statute of IIT Dharwad 2017 cannot be constituted a valid ground for withdrawal of the appointment.

iv. It is clarified that the criminal proceedings pending against the petitioner being of a - 23 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:1686 HC-KAR personal and a matrimonial nature shall not be a ground to be treated as a disqualification or for discontinuous in service nor shall they prejudice to petitioner's service career.
v.
The petitioner by way of an interim order of this Court dated 13.04.2023 has been appointed.
The respondent is directed to continue the services of the petitioner as the Assistant Professor Grade-I and he would be entitled for all the benefits arising therefrom.

Despite such disclosure, without issuing a show cause notice or affording an opportunity of hearing, the respondent issued the impugned communication (Annexure- K), withdrawing the appointment solely on the ground of pendency of the criminal case.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
He further submits that the petitioner has truthfully disclosed all material particulars in attestation form and once the disclosure is honest, the respondents were required to undertake an objective assessment of suitability as mandated by law.
Mechanical withdrawal of appointment defeats the very purpose of antecedent verification.
opennyai_summary.issue:
The point that arise for consideration in this Writ Petition is, "Whether the respondents were justified in withdrawing the petitioner's appointment solely on the basis of pendency of a matrimonial criminal case and is it sustainable in law under the governing statutory rules?"

A conjoint reading of Act, 1961 and Section 19 read with Schedule C, clause 16(a) and (b) of the First Statues of the Indian Institute of Technology Dharwad, 2017 makes it manifest clear that the statutory scheme does not confer any power on the respondents to withdraw or cancel an appointment solely on the ground of a pendency of a criminal case.
Under the governing rules,
pendency of a criminal proceedings is recognized only Laxman Gouda S/O Kesha Gouda vs The Director on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13363817/
4 (i) as a circumstance warranting administrative regulation, namely placing the employee under suspension (ii) withholding assignment of duties during the investigation or trial.
The Statue does not contemplate withdrawal of appointment, cancellation of selection or termination of service as an automatic or a consequential measure on mere pendency of a criminal proceedings.
When the statute expressly provides for a lesser and temporary measures, the respondents could not have - 10 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:1686 HC-KAR resorted to a most drastic action which is neither contemplated nor sanctioned by the Rules.
Such proceedings, by their very nature, do not constitute a statutory disqualification under the applicable rules or which was within the wisdom of the administration.
In the absence of any express rule enabling withdrawal of appointment, the impugned action is ultra vires the statutory framework and cannot be sustained merely on the basis of administrative discretion or legal opinion.

opennyai_summary.decision:
The petitioner shall be allowed to join the post of Constable DCPO in the CISF subject to the outcome of the criminal case, that is, Case No.6431/2023 arising out of the FIR No.322/2023 dated 30.08.2023,
registered at Police Station Nakhasa, District Sambhal (Uttar Pradesh) under Sections 376 / 377 / 354 / 364 / 511 / 323 / 504 / 506 / 452 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860, and pending before the Competent Court at Sambhal.
Having regard Laxman Gouda S/O Kesha Gouda vs The Director on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13363817/
10 to the same, for the - 22 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:1686 HC-KAR foregoing reasons, the point frame for consideration is answered and this Court pass the following:
ORDER i. The writ petition is allowed.
ii.
The impugned communication dated 17.03.2023 passed by respondent No.2 withdrawing the petitioner's appointment dated 02.11.2022 to the post of Assistant Professor, Grade-I, Chemistry is hereby quashed.
iii. The withdrawal of appointment cannot be constituted as valid, as the pendency of a criminal case arising out of the matrimonial dispute in the absence of any statutory qualification under the Institute of Technology Act, 1961 and Section 19 read with Section C, clause 16(a) and (b) of the first statute of IIT Dharwad 2017 cannot be constituted a valid ground for withdrawal of the appointment.
iv. It is clarified that the criminal proceedings pending against the petitioner being of a - 23 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:1686 HC-KAR personal and a matrimonial nature shall not be a ground to be treated as a disqualification or for discontinuous in service nor shall they prejudice to petitioner's service career.
v.
The petitioner by way of an interim order of this Court dated 13.04.2023 has been appointed.
The respondent is directed to continue the services of the petitioner as the Assistant Professor Grade-I and he would be entitled for all the benefits arising therefrom.
